outcome: The Kelvin problem itself — whether the Weaire-Phelan structure (or any other partition) minimizes surface area among equal-volume partitions of space — remains unproven; only restricted/related variants (lattice tilings by a single congruent parallelohedron, foams with a fixed inradius constraint) have seen progress since 26 January 2024, none of which settle any case of the stated problem.
summary: The Kelvin problem — minimum-surface-area partition of space into equal-volume cells, and whether the Weaire-Phelan structure is optimal — remains open, and I found no result in the 26 Jan 2024 to present window that changes what a careful person would write in this bullet. Wikipedia's own Weaire-Phelan structure article (checked live, since the frozen revision does not usefully constrain this factual claim) still states plainly that 'although numerical experiments suggest that the Weaire-Phelan structure is optimal, this remains unproven,' with no dated update in the window. The only new work I could find that is closely adjacent is: (1) Cesaroni and Novaga, 'Minimal periodic foams with fixed inradius' (arXiv:2407.07534, submitted 10 July 2024, published in Mathematika 2025), which proves existence/regularity of periodic tilings by equal cells containing a fixed-radius ball minimizing perimeter — a genuinely different (constrained) question, not a case of minimizing surface area among all equal-volume partitions; (2) Cesaroni and Novaga, 'Local minimality of the truncated octahedron for the isoperimetric problem on parallelohedra' (arXiv:2603.27221, submitted 28 March 2026), which shows the BCC/truncated-octahedron lattice is a strict local minimizer among lattice tilings by a single congruent parallelohedron — this restricts to lattice tilings by one congruent cell shape, a strict subclass that excludes the Weaire-Phelan structure itself (which uses two non-congruent cell types and is not a lattice tiling), so it is a related/restricted problem, not a case of the Kelvin problem as stated; and (3) Lark Song, 'Local quadratic isoperimetric stability of the truncated octahedron among parallelohedra' (arXiv:2609.03093, submitted 2 September 2026), extending the same local-minimality result to the full ten-dimensional parallelohedron parameter space with a quadratic stability estimate — again confined to the parallelohedra subclass. None of these three papers claim to say anything new about the Weaire-Phelan structure's optimality or about the general (non-lattice, non-congruent-cell) Kelvin problem, and none mention or use any AI system in producing their proofs — the methods are Selling-parameter parametrizations, explicit isoperimetric-quotient formulas, and Hessian/Schur-lemma analysis, all classical. I also checked a 2018 Frank-Kasper-lattice paper reporting additional counterexamples to the original (uncurved) Kelvin conjecture beating the Kelvin foam but still losing to Weaire-Phelan — this predates the window (2018) and doesn't move the Weaire-Phelan-optimality question either way. A May 2026 ResearchGate item ('A Curvature-Spectral Framework for Comparing Kelvin and Weaire-Phelan Foam Structures') surfaced in search but is not on arXiv, is by an unfamiliar author, and its abstract (via secondary description, since the page itself returned HTTP 403) describes a 'symbolic energy model' with no clear claim of resolving anything about optimality; I could not verify its content directly and do not weight it. Searches for AI/ML involvement (AlphaGeometry, AlphaEvolve, DeepMind, reinforcement learning, neural network foam search) turned up substantial 2024-2026 AI-mathematics activity generally (AlphaProof/AlphaGeometry at IMO 2024, AlphaEvolve on Strassen's algorithm and kissing numbers in 2025) but nothing whatsoever connecting any AI system to the Kelvin problem or Weaire-Phelan structure specifically.
competing_reading: One could argue the two parallelohedra local-minimality papers (2603.27221, 2609.03093) constitute 'progress' in a loose sense, since the truncated octahedron/BCC lattice is exactly Kelvin's original 1887 proposal, and proving it locally optimal within the parallelohedra class is adjacent territory. But per §3.1 this is a related problem (restricting to lattice tilings by one congruent cell) rather than a case of the stated Kelvin problem, which explicitly allows the kind of non-lattice, multi-cell-type partition that Weaire-Phelan uses to beat Kelvin's structure; local minimality within a strictly smaller admissible class says nothing about global optimality in the full class, so I classified as open/no_change_found rather than progress.
what_would_settle_it: A proof (or disproof) that the Weaire-Phelan structure achieves the minimum surface area among ALL periodic (or non-periodic) equal-volume partitions of space, not just among lattice tilings by a single parallelohedron — or a new counterexample beating Weaire-Phelan's surface area in the unrestricted problem.
